research_notes: Current strict protocol is intentionally conservative about classification but aggressive about coarse target ascent.
That combination finds the region quickly without promoting unreliable operating limits.
Once the first failed upper class appears, one-minute refinement is sufficient for the current operational objective.
Sub-minute boundary precision would likely be false precision given provider/runtime variance.
Safety margin should absorb observed variance rather than relying on overly precise cutoff estimates.
The final policy should therefore be robust to timing noise rather than tuned to a single exact second.
